decisions.chosen: Kernel-owned observer registry invoking method Callables; no engine signals for kernel-to-subscriber notification; acceptance gated on KRN-LAT-02 release-export notify cost, reopen (no automatic fallback) if it fails
decisions.reason: Decided on semantics: handler must return the completion token (per-subscriber INCOMPLETE), two class cadences, DEAD_SUBSCRIBER counting, per-block filtering. Cost does not discriminate (probed 2026-10-28 on the editor build: Callable.call 155 ns vs signal emit 157 ns at 10 subscribers). This is the kernel GDD's lean.

decisions.chosen: Per block: subscribe(cls, block_id, handler, name); wildcard &"*" for DIAGNOSTIC only; two blocks means two subscriptions
decisions.reason: Layout LY-32 already assumes per-block subscription; cost scales with dirty blocks, a quiet tick makes zero calls (KRN-PERF-01). The architecture sketch's two-argument form is a gdd_sync item.

decisions.chosen: (batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken, return ctx.complete() last; INCOMPLETE recorded per subscription without faulting
decisions.reason: ADR-0003 names NotifyContext for subscriber handlers and forbids void-returning kernel-invoked callables; the kernel GDD AC requires the sentinel. The architecture example (void, Dictionary.merge) is stale.

decisions.chosen: Only standard method Callables (is_standard()); lambdas and .bind() results refused with SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED
decisions.reason: Probed 2026-10-28: both are is_custom(); a lambda's get_object() is the script not the creator, so the block-or-hook-owner check cannot see through it, and lambdas capturing self leak (ADR-0002 already bans them for result handlers).

decisions.chosen: Keep CR-10's five classes; PER_TICK for INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION, FRAME_MERGED for PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR, DIAGNOSTIC; DIAGNOSTIC gated by the dev predicate, REPLICATION by replication_enabled (false at MVP); ADR-0009 owns read/write rights
decisions.reason: Ratified R-12; keeps this ADR to delivery properties and leaves ADR-0009 and ADR-0002 their scope.

decisions.chosen: Deferred application of subscribe, unsubscribe and prune at the next delivery boundary instead of copying the list each P5
decisions.reason: Identical observable behaviour (KRN-NOT-02) with zero per-tick allocation.

decisions.chosen: 64-bit int (KIND << 32) | id, KIND 1..0x7FFF declared per block, id 32 bits (0 for singleton families), keys block-local, NO_KEY = INT64_MAX sentinel, ALL as a batch flag is_all
decisions.reason: All owner GDDs already use it; the 0x7FFF cap keeps keys below 2^47 (exact as float) and strictly below NO_KEY (probed: kind 0x7FFFFFFF with a full id equals INT64_MAX); no key value is spent on ALL.

decisions.chosen: New BlockRegistrar.register_key_space(KeySpaceDescriptor) with kind_ids/names, event_ids/names and quiet_writes_allowed, mandatory per block
decisions.reason: Needed for printable diagnostics, STRICT_DEBUG kind checks and to state which blocks may legally write without a key; follows CR-6 no-silent-defaults.

decisions.chosen: Fixed PackedInt64Array per block per cadence, has() native scan for dedupe, count, is_all on the (capacity+1)th distinct key, native sort at P4 close; open-addressed set kept as documented fallback
decisions.reason: Probed 2026-10-28: 160-230 ns/mark, 52 us for 256 distinct keys, OBJECT_COUNT flat, exact 256 vs 257 behaviour; Dictionary set allocates and is iterated; fallback only if KRN-LAT-02 shows a release-export problem.

decisions.chosen: Buffers sized at the registry freeze; runtime changes may only lower it, effective at next tick's P0; raising above the sized capacity is KNOB_REFUSED
decisions.reason: Keeps buffers fixed-size for the whole run and satisfies the AC that a change during P2 of T takes effect at T+1.

decisions.chosen: Reused facade over the kernel's closed buffer with key(i)/has(key)/event(i); keys ascending and unique; valid only during the handler call (poisoned under STRICT_DEBUG); no array handed out
decisions.reason: Packed arrays pass by reference and cannot be read-only (ADR-0007 B2); copying per delivery would allocate; sorted canonical order makes HOST and MIRROR batches comparable.

decisions.chosen: Provide DirtyAccumulator (absorb, has, key, clear, is_all) built on the same KeyBuf code, capacity from NotifyFacet.key_capacity
decisions.reason: FT-15 and every PRESENTATION system need the same union and collapse; architecture's Dictionary.merge example cannot work with a packed array. ADR-0009 owns how it is used.

decisions.chosen: NotifyEvent (kind + up to six ints, pooled) emitted by scope.emit_event(block_id, kind, a0..a5); delivered inside the emitting block's batch to every subscription of that block; concatenated, never unioned, in a catch-up frame; MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK 64, overflow EVENT_OVERFLOW
decisions.reason: TR-shipbody-027 and TR-webmap-023 need ints-only events; BODY_TRANSFER has exactly six ints once the sub-kind folds into the kind; riding the block's batch avoids a second channel and subscription.

decisions.chosen: Per block tick buffer folded into a frame buffer at P5 (swap when the frame buffer is empty, else union; past capacity is_all); merged classes delivered once by Kernel.deliver_frame_end(), the last step of TickDriver.frame on every exit path; tick = last committed tick, first_tick also exposed
decisions.reason: Implements ratified R-12 and KRN-NOT-01 (early exit covers committed ticks only; a faulting tick contributes nothing); needs an ADR-0001 step.

decisions.chosen: On LOADING to RUNNING, deliver_all() clears every buffer and event list then delivers one ALL batch per registered block to every subscription of every class at the restored T; INIT/RESTORE marks and events are discarded
decisions.reason: Consumes ADR-0003's 'dirty in INIT/RESTORE is discarded, one ALL per block instead' and the GDD's 'one ALL then silence'; a pending merged union is superseded by the replaced world.

decisions.chosen: Treated as a pseudo-tick with tick = T: per-tick classes at its P5, merged classes at that frame's deliver_frame_end()
decisions.reason: The cycle runs P4 and P5 with T unchanged; no special channel needed.

decisions.chosen: Always-on touch_serial per block (set by every granted open_for) plus a dev/test audit riding the SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE's pre-P5 hash (no extra hash pass): MISSED_DIRTY_MARK when the hash changed, the serial advanced, no key or ALL was marked and the block's key space has quiet_writes_allowed == false; every-tick in tests (AUDIT_EVERY_TICK), sampled at TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS 60 in dev builds
decisions.reason: A literal 'changed block must mark a key' check is wrong for Graph (LS-20 bucketed), Emitter (pose never dirties) and Web Map (zero keys per leg); quiet blocks get per-mutator exact-key tests and a QUIET_WRITE_TICKS counter instead. Marked-but-unchanged is not a violation. Release exports detect nothing at run time (accepted).

decisions.point: Touch serial and the hash cache
decisions.chosen: Expose touch_serial and recommend it to ADR-0005 for cache invalidation; do not impose it
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 is a parallel sibling; D.12 says the cache is diagnostics-only (all determinism checks hash uncached) so the stake is a stale diagnostics value. The D.12 wording sync is conditional on ADR-0005.

decisions.chosen: Evaluated at subscribe time and re-evaluated at the registry freeze for earlier subscriptions; a hit at the freeze removes the subscription with SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED (not a boot fault); an unknown block name at the freeze is a boot fault UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY
decisions.reason: Presentation setup() may precede owner registration during BOOTING; a typo in a block name that silently never fires is worse than a boot failure.

decisions.chosen: SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DIRTY_KEY_INVALID, DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED, EVENT_OVERFLOW, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK added to ADR-0003's closed violation set; MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS 96 and MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK 64 as Boot knobs
decisions.reason: ADR-0003's set omitted SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED although the kernel GDD AC requires it; the rest are this ADR's new counters.

decisions.chosen: Proposal of 0.25 ms P99 for P5 plus frame-end delivery on a defined stress workload, labelled a proposal pending KRN-LAT-02, not a GDD number
decisions.reason: The kernel GDD defines t_P5 but no budget; indicative editor-build costs are far below it.

decisions.chosen: Follow the registry (presentation_submit_without_handle): subscribing as INPUT_SURFACE confers no submit right; the GDD AC is a sync item
decisions.reason: Registry stances are binding; ADR-0002 states the same rule.

decisions.point: Sim-side event consumers and Save/Load triggers
decisions.chosen: Do not add a HOST_SERVICE class or a sim-side event feed; recommend Attention, Horror and Save/Load read owner views (Save/Load per architecture rule 3); recorded as open questions
decisions.reason: CR-10 forbids block and hook owners from subscribing and its class table is closed; the choice belongs to the Web Map, Attention, Horror and Save/Load owners and ADR-0006/0009.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: TickDriver.frame calls Kernel.deliver_frame_end() as its last step on every exit path (zero-tick frame, early exit by pause/restore/fault, paused frame), after the result flush and the paused service cycle; NotifyFacet is issued by the composition root; simulation setup() calls (block registration, key spaces) complete before presentation subscriptions are resolved at the freeze, though a subscription made earlier is accepted and resolved at the freeze.
Subscribing as INPUT_SURFACE confers no submit right (SurfaceHandle issued separately); result handlers are method Callables, the same rule applied here to subscriber handlers.

WriteScope gains emit_event(block_id, kind, a0..a5); BlockRegistrar gains register_key_space(KeySpaceDescriptor); the closed violation set gains SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DIRTY_KEY_INVALID, DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED, EVENT_OVERFLOW, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK; UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY also covers an unknown subscription block; mark_dirty requires a prior granted open_for for that block in the same scope use; touch_serial joins the H1 registries allow-list; INIT/RESTORE marks discarded exactly as ADR-0003 section 4 states; NotifyContext is reused and re-armed per subscriber call; SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE takes a per-block hash just before P5 that the audit reuses.

block_hash(block_id, uncached = true) exists for persist blocks (kernel GDD D.12) and may be called at the pre-P5 point (not inside an open WriteScope on that block); ADR-0005 decides whether the per-block hash cache is invalidated by Kernel.touch_serial(block_index) (recommended) or by dirty keys; a hash for non-persist blocks is not assumed.

Restore and new game end in the kernel transition LOADING to RUNNING, which triggers deliver_all(); Save/Load consumes pod-arrival and berth autosave triggers by polling owner read views (architecture rule 3) rather than by subscribing; it needs no new subscriber class.

Presentation subscribers use ChangeBatch and DirtyAccumulator as defined here; ADR-0009 owns what each class may read and write, the handler discipline (mark dirty only, draw in the render callback), which keys fire when (TR-emitter-026, TR-light-007, TR-attention-026 polling), and any subscribe-time rule restricting who may attach to a PERCEPTION_OUT block.

ADR-0010 decides which guidelines are statically lintable (no signal declarations or connect() on kernel objects in src/kernel; no String/float key construction; no lambda subscribers via regex where possible) versus runtime-checked here (is_standard check, STRICT_DEBUG kind check, batch poisoning); the zero-allocation claims here are verified by OBJECT_COUNT flat plus is_same identity checks, as in ADR-0007.

The dev predicate that gates DIAGNOSTIC subscriptions is set by the composition root; the diagnostics accessor surfaces the new counters (SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DEAD_SUBSCRIBER, EVENT_OVERFLOW, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK, per-block QUIET_WRITE_TICKS) and the wildcard DIAGNOSTIC subscription is the Debug Overlay's entry point.

REPLICATION is a PER_TICK class refused unless replication_enabled (false at MVP); batches carry no state, so the replication shape does not change the key encoding; keys are canonical (sorted, unique) so HOST and MIRROR batches compare equal.

The Graph key kinds are COMP 1 .. SECTION 9 as LS-20 states, quiet_writes_allowed = true, and composite family ids such as L/<loop>/<anchor> are packed into the 32-bit id by the Graph; each Core owner ADR (0011, 0013, 0015, 0017, 0019) numbers its own unnumbered families and registers its key space.

open_questions: P5 budget: the kernel GDD defines t_P5 but no budget; 0.25 ms P99 is this ADR's proposal. KRN-LAT-02 on a release export (RM-DESKTOP, RM-DECK) sets the real figure, measures the 256-distinct has() worst case and confirms the registry shows no cost problem (the OQ-4 gate). All timings in the ADR are editor-build probes, indicative only.

Sim-side event consumers: WM-31 lists Attention and Horror as consumers of Web Map events, but CR-10 forbids block and hook owners from subscribing. ADR assumes they read web.state's view in their hooks; Web Map, Attention and Horror owners must confirm. horror-entities.md ~L369 ('load and unload events') was not read for this ADR.

Save/Load trigger path: POD_ARRIVED and BERTHED are autosave triggers but no CR-10 class fits a host service. Recommended: poll an owner read view; if a subscription is wanted, ADR-0006 or ADR-0009 must name the class (a HOST_SERVICE class was considered and not adopted).

Conflict surfaced, not papered over: kernel GDD AC ~L1014 says subscribe returns a submit handle only to INPUT_SURFACE, while registry presentation_submit_without_handle (ADR-0002) says subscribing confers nothing. The registry wins; the GDD AC needs rewording. ADR-0003's closed violation set also omitted SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, which the same AC requires.

Hash-cache invalidation: ADR-0004 exposes touch_serial and recommends it to ADR-0005 because a quantised write (Graph LS-20, Emitter EM-26, Web Map WM-2) changes a block without marking a key. ADR-0005 decides; the D.12 wording sync is conditional on it. D.12 makes the cache diagnostics-only, so the stake is a stale diagnostics value.

The missed-mark audit covers only persist blocks (block_hash returns BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN for non-persist blocks) and cannot see a wrong key of a declared kind; quiet_writes_allowed blocks (Graph, Emitter, Body, Suit, Controller, Sanity) are covered only by per-mutator exact-key tests and the QUIET_WRITE_TICKS counter. Release exports detect nothing at run time. ADR-0005 may offer a hash for non-persist blocks.

Kind numbers for Emitter, Suit, Web Map, Attention and Controller families are unnumbered in their GDDs; each owner ADR fixes them (distinct within a block); a CI key-space consistency test per owner is specified.
Graph composite family L/<loop>/<anchor> must pack into the 32-bit id; ADR-0011 fixes the packing and range check.
PERCEPTION_OUT block batches (sanity.perception) should reach only the Perception Filter and Debug; delivery here is class-based, so a subscribe-time rule belongs to ADR-0009 or ADR-0024.

UNVERIFIED engine facts (settled by KRN-LAT-02 and ADR-0003's KRN-CTX-06 on a release export): PackedInt64Array.has/sort/bsearch/fill release-template cost; that signals emit in connection order (never relied on); behaviour of a subscriber that aborts on a script error in release; typed Dictionary[StringName, int] (4.4, post-cutoff) with a plain-Dictionary fallback.
Six event integers fit every current GDD payload (BODY_TRANSFER is exactly six after splitting weld/detach/pod into three event kinds); a longer payload needs a seventh slot or a second event.

A fault leaves half-applied blocks visible through read views with no notification (the faulting tick's marks are discarded per KRN-NOT-01); accepted because the fault screen replaces the play view, but worth confirming with the presentation owners.
Joint review pending: engine specialist and technical director have not reviewed this ADR; Review Log reads 'pending (joint review)'.

data.summary: ADR-0004 (Proposed, 2026-10-28) fixes change notification as a kernel-owned observer registry (not engine signals) that delivers per-block (ChangeBatch: block, tick, sorted unique int keys or is_all, events) to five subscriber classes with per-tick (INPUT_SURFACE, REPLICATION) and frame-merged (PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR, DIAGNOSTIC) cadences, plus one ALL batch per block on LOADING to RUNNING. Dirty keys are 64-bit ints (KIND << 32) | id (KIND 1..0x7FFF, declared per block via a KeySpaceDescriptor), collected allocation-free in the write scope into a fixed PackedInt64Array per block with has() dedupe and exact collapse at MAX_DIRTY_KEYS, with a dev/test-only missed-mark audit built on a touch serial; acceptance is gated on KRN-LAT-02 notify cost on a release export.

registry_candidates.name: change_notification
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- contract: change_notification
    status: active           # ADR-0004 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call     # kernel-owned observer registry invoking method Callables; not engine signals
    producer: command-simulation-layer (kernel P5 and frame-end delivery)
    consumers:

registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: notification_transport
    status: active           # ADR-0004 is Proposed; KRN-LAT-02 notify cost gates acceptance
    api: "kernel-owned subscription registry; per-block subscriptions; Callable.call(batch, ctx) on method Callables guarded by is_valid(); subscribe and unsubscribe applied at the next delivery boundary"

registry_candidates.name: kernel_signal_notification
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: kernel_signal_notification
    status: active           # ADR-0004 is Proposed
    description: "No engine signal carries kernel-to-subscriber change notification: src/kernel declares no signal for it, nothing connect()s to a kernel object, and subscribers register only through NotifyFacet.subscribe. Engine signals remain legal inside presentation."
    why: "A signal returns nothing (no completion token, no per-subscriber INCOMPLETE), has no class cadence or block filter, and hides dead subscribers; OQ-4 decided on semantics."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0004-change-notification-and-dirty-keys.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: lambda_or_retained_batch_subscriber
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: lambda_or_retained_batch_subscriber
    status: active           # ADR-0004 is Proposed
    description: "A subscriber handler is a standard method Callable on a long-lived object with the signature (batch, ctx) -> CompletionToken; never a lambda or .bind() result, and never retains a ChangeBatch, a kernel key buffer or an event object past the handler call (copy into a DirtyAccumulator)."
    why: "Probed 2026-10-28: lambdas and bind results are custom Callables whose get_object() does not identify the owner and which keep self alive; the batch is a reused facade re-armed every delivery."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0004-change-notification-and-dirty-keys.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: non_integer_or_undeclared_dirty_key
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: non_integer_or_undeclared_dirty_key
    status: active           # ADR-0004 is Proposed
    description: "A dirty key is an int (KIND << 32) | id built from integers, KIND declared in the block's KeySpaceDescriptor; never a String, StringName, float or Variant, never an id above 32 bits, never key 0 or NO_KEY; events carry only ints and never state."
    why: "No String is built per key per run (Graph LS-20, ADR-LSG-06); NO_KEY is the buffer sentinel; notifications carry no state (CR-10)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0004-change-notification-and-dirty-keys.md
    added: 2026-10-28

decisions.chosen: Kernel-owned observer registry invoking method Callables; no engine signals for kernel-to-subscriber notification; acceptance gated on KRN-LAT-02 release-export notify cost, reopen (no automatic fallback) if it fails
decisions.reason: Decided on semantics: handler must return the completion token (per-subscriber INCOMPLETE), two class cadences, DEAD_SUBSCRIBER counting, per-block filtering. Cost does not discriminate (probed 2026-10-28 on the editor build: Callable.call 155 ns vs signal emit 157 ns at 10 subscribers). This is the kernel GDD's lean.

decisions.chosen: Per block: subscribe(cls, block_id, handler, name); wildcard &"*" for DIAGNOSTIC only; two blocks means two subscriptions
decisions.reason: Layout LY-32 already assumes per-block subscription; cost scales with dirty blocks, a quiet tick makes zero calls (KRN-PERF-01). The architecture sketch's two-argument form is a gdd_sync item.

decisions.chosen: (batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken, return ctx.complete() last; INCOMPLETE recorded per subscription without faulting
decisions.reason: ADR-0003 names NotifyContext for subscriber handlers and forbids void-returning kernel-invoked callables; the kernel GDD AC requires the sentinel. The architecture example (void, Dictionary.merge) is stale.

decisions.chosen: Only standard method Callables (is_standard()); lambdas and .bind() results refused with SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED
decisions.reason: Probed 2026-10-28: both are is_custom(); a lambda's get_object() is the script not the creator, so the block-or-hook-owner check cannot see through it, and lambdas capturing self leak (ADR-0002 already bans them for result handlers).

decisions.chosen: Keep CR-10's five classes; PER_TICK for INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION, FRAME_MERGED for PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR, DIAGNOSTIC; DIAGNOSTIC gated by the dev predicate, REPLICATION by replication_enabled (false at MVP); ADR-0009 owns read/write rights
decisions.reason: Ratified R-12; keeps this ADR to delivery properties and leaves ADR-0009 and ADR-0002 their scope.

decisions.chosen: Deferred application of subscribe, unsubscribe and prune at the next delivery boundary instead of copying the list each P5
decisions.reason: Identical observable behaviour (KRN-NOT-02) with zero per-tick allocation.

decisions.chosen: 64-bit int (KIND << 32) | id, KIND 1..0x7FFF declared per block, id 32 bits (0 for singleton families), keys block-local, NO_KEY = INT64_MAX sentinel, ALL as a batch flag is_all
decisions.reason: All owner GDDs already use it; the 0x7FFF cap keeps keys below 2^47 (exact as float) and strictly below NO_KEY (probed: kind 0x7FFFFFFF with a full id equals INT64_MAX); no key value is spent on ALL.

decisions.chosen: New BlockRegistrar.register_key_space(KeySpaceDescriptor) with kind_ids/names, event_ids/names and quiet_writes_allowed, mandatory per block
decisions.reason: Needed for printable diagnostics, STRICT_DEBUG kind checks and to state which blocks may legally write without a key; follows CR-6 no-silent-defaults.

decisions.chosen: Fixed PackedInt64Array per block per cadence, has() native scan for dedupe, count, is_all on the (capacity+1)th distinct key, native sort at P4 close; open-addressed set kept as documented fallback
decisions.reason: Probed 2026-10-28: 160-230 ns/mark, 52 us for 256 distinct keys, OBJECT_COUNT flat, exact 256 vs 257 behaviour; Dictionary set allocates and is iterated; fallback only if KRN-LAT-02 shows a release-export problem.

decisions.chosen: Buffers sized at the registry freeze; runtime changes may only lower it, effective at next tick's P0; raising above the sized capacity is KNOB_REFUSED
decisions.reason: Keeps buffers fixed-size for the whole run and satisfies the AC that a change during P2 of T takes effect at T+1.

decisions.chosen: Reused facade over the kernel's closed buffer with key(i)/has(key)/event(i); keys ascending and unique; valid only during the handler call (poisoned under STRICT_DEBUG); no array handed out
decisions.reason: Packed arrays pass by reference and cannot be read-only (ADR-0007 B2); copying per delivery would allocate; sorted canonical order makes HOST and MIRROR batches comparable.

decisions.chosen: Provide DirtyAccumulator (absorb, has, key, clear, is_all) built on the same KeyBuf code, capacity from NotifyFacet.key_capacity
decisions.reason: FT-15 and every PRESENTATION system need the same union and collapse; architecture's Dictionary.merge example cannot work with a packed array. ADR-0009 owns how it is used.

decisions.chosen: NotifyEvent (kind + up to six ints, pooled) emitted by scope.emit_event(block_id, kind, a0..a5); delivered inside the emitting block's batch to every subscription of that block; concatenated, never unioned, in a catch-up frame; MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK 64, overflow EVENT_OVERFLOW
decisions.reason: TR-shipbody-027 and TR-webmap-023 need ints-only events; BODY_TRANSFER has exactly six ints once the sub-kind folds into the kind; riding the block's batch avoids a second channel and subscription.

decisions.chosen: Per block tick buffer folded into a frame buffer at P5 (swap when the frame buffer is empty, else union; past capacity is_all); merged classes delivered once by Kernel.deliver_frame_end(), the last step of TickDriver.frame on every exit path; tick = last committed tick, first_tick also exposed
decisions.reason: Implements ratified R-12 and KRN-NOT-01 (early exit covers committed ticks only; a faulting tick contributes nothing); needs an ADR-0001 step.

decisions.chosen: On LOADING to RUNNING, deliver_all() clears every buffer and event list then delivers one ALL batch per registered block to every subscription of every class at the restored T; INIT/RESTORE marks and events are discarded
decisions.reason: Consumes ADR-0003's 'dirty in INIT/RESTORE is discarded, one ALL per block instead' and the GDD's 'one ALL then silence'; a pending merged union is superseded by the replaced world.

decisions.chosen: Treated as a pseudo-tick with tick = T: per-tick classes at its P5, merged classes at that frame's deliver_frame_end()
decisions.reason: The cycle runs P4 and P5 with T unchanged; no special channel needed.

decisions.chosen: Always-on touch_serial per block (set by every granted open_for) plus a dev/test audit riding the SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE's pre-P5 hash (no extra hash pass): MISSED_DIRTY_MARK when the hash changed, the serial advanced, no key or ALL was marked and the block's key space has quiet_writes_allowed == false; every-tick in tests (AUDIT_EVERY_TICK), sampled at TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS 60 in dev builds
decisions.reason: A literal 'changed block must mark a key' check is wrong for Graph (LS-20 bucketed), Emitter (pose never dirties) and Web Map (zero keys per leg); quiet blocks get per-mutator exact-key tests and a QUIET_WRITE_TICKS counter instead. Marked-but-unchanged is not a violation. Release exports detect nothing at run time (accepted).

decisions.point: Touch serial and the hash cache
decisions.chosen: Expose touch_serial and recommend it to ADR-0005 for cache invalidation; do not impose it
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 is a parallel sibling; D.12 says the cache is diagnostics-only (all determinism checks hash uncached) so the stake is a stale diagnostics value. The D.12 wording sync is conditional on ADR-0005.

decisions.chosen: Evaluated at subscribe time and re-evaluated at the registry freeze for earlier subscriptions; a hit at the freeze removes the subscription with SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED (not a boot fault); an unknown block name at the freeze is a boot fault UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY
decisions.reason: Presentation setup() may precede owner registration during BOOTING; a typo in a block name that silently never fires is worse than a boot failure.

decisions.chosen: SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DIRTY_KEY_INVALID, DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED, EVENT_OVERFLOW, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK added to ADR-0003's closed violation set; MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS 96 and MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK 64 as Boot knobs
decisions.reason: ADR-0003's set omitted SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED although the kernel GDD AC requires it; the rest are this ADR's new counters.

decisions.chosen: Proposal of 0.25 ms P99 for P5 plus frame-end delivery on a defined stress workload, labelled a proposal pending KRN-LAT-02, not a GDD number
decisions.reason: The kernel GDD defines t_P5 but no budget; indicative editor-build costs are far below it.

decisions.chosen: Follow the registry (presentation_submit_without_handle): subscribing as INPUT_SURFACE confers no submit right; the GDD AC is a sync item
decisions.reason: Registry stances are binding; ADR-0002 states the same rule.

decisions.point: Sim-side event consumers and Save/Load triggers
decisions.chosen: Do not add a HOST_SERVICE class or a sim-side event feed; recommend Attention, Horror and Save/Load read owner views (Save/Load per architecture rule 3); recorded as open questions
decisions.reason: CR-10 forbids block and hook owners from subscribing and its class table is closed; the choice belongs to the Web Map, Attention, Horror and Save/Load owners and ADR-0006/0009.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: TickDriver.frame calls Kernel.deliver_frame_end() as its last step on every exit path (zero-tick frame, early exit by pause/restore/fault, paused frame), after the result flush and the paused service cycle; NotifyFacet is issued by the composition root; simulation setup() calls (block registration, key spaces) complete before presentation subscriptions are resolved at the freeze, though a subscription made earlier is accepted and resolved at the freeze.
Subscribing as INPUT_SURFACE confers no submit right (SurfaceHandle issued separately); result handlers are method Callables, the same rule applied here to subscriber handlers.

WriteScope gains emit_event(block_id, kind, a0..a5); BlockRegistrar gains register_key_space(KeySpaceDescriptor); the closed violation set gains SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DIRTY_KEY_INVALID, DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED, EVENT_OVERFLOW, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK; UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY also covers an unknown subscription block; mark_dirty requires a prior granted open_for for that block in the same scope use; touch_serial joins the H1 registries allow-list; INIT/RESTORE marks discarded exactly as ADR-0003 section 4 states; NotifyContext is reused and re-armed per subscriber call; SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE takes a per-block hash just before P5 that the audit reuses.

block_hash(block_id, uncached = true) exists for persist blocks (kernel GDD D.12) and may be called at the pre-P5 point (not inside an open WriteScope on that block); ADR-0005 decides whether the per-block hash cache is invalidated by Kernel.touch_serial(block_index) (recommended) or by dirty keys; a hash for non-persist blocks is not assumed.

Restore and new game end in the kernel transition LOADING to RUNNING, which triggers deliver_all(); Save/Load consumes pod-arrival and berth autosave triggers by polling owner read views (architecture rule 3) rather than by subscribing; it needs no new subscriber class.

Presentation subscribers use ChangeBatch and DirtyAccumulator as defined here; ADR-0009 owns what each class may read and write, the handler discipline (mark dirty only, draw in the render callback), which keys fire when (TR-emitter-026, TR-light-007, TR-attention-026 polling), and any subscribe-time rule restricting who may attach to a PERCEPTION_OUT block.

ADR-0010 decides which guidelines are statically lintable (no signal declarations or connect() on kernel objects in src/kernel; no String/float key construction; no lambda subscribers via regex where possible) versus runtime-checked here (is_standard check, STRICT_DEBUG kind check, batch poisoning); the zero-allocation claims here are verified by OBJECT_COUNT flat plus is_same identity checks, as in ADR-0007.

The dev predicate that gates DIAGNOSTIC subscriptions is set by the composition root; the diagnostics accessor surfaces the new counters (SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DEAD_SUBSCRIBER, EVENT_OVERFLOW, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK, per-block QUIET_WRITE_TICKS) and the wildcard DIAGNOSTIC subscription is the Debug Overlay's entry point.

REPLICATION is a PER_TICK class refused unless replication_enabled (false at MVP); batches carry no state, so the replication shape does not change the key encoding; keys are canonical (sorted, unique) so HOST and MIRROR batches compare equal.

The Graph key kinds are COMP 1 .. SECTION 9 as LS-20 states, quiet_writes_allowed = true, and composite family ids such as L/<loop>/<anchor> are packed into the 32-bit id by the Graph; each Core owner ADR (0011, 0013, 0015, 0017, 0019) numbers its own unnumbered families and registers its key space.

open_questions: P5 budget: the kernel GDD defines t_P5 but no budget; 0.25 ms P99 is this ADR's proposal. KRN-LAT-02 on a release export (RM-DESKTOP, RM-DECK) sets the real figure, measures the 256-distinct has() worst case and confirms the registry shows no cost problem (the OQ-4 gate). All timings in the ADR are editor-build probes, indicative only.

Sim-side event consumers: WM-31 lists Attention and Horror as consumers of Web Map events, but CR-10 forbids block and hook owners from subscribing. ADR assumes they read web.state's view in their hooks; Web Map, Attention and Horror owners must confirm. horror-entities.md ~L369 ('load and unload events') was not read for this ADR.

Save/Load trigger path: POD_ARRIVED and BERTHED are autosave triggers but no CR-10 class fits a host service. Recommended: poll an owner read view; if a subscription is wanted, ADR-0006 or ADR-0009 must name the class (a HOST_SERVICE class was considered and not adopted).

Conflict surfaced, not papered over: kernel GDD AC ~L1014 says subscribe returns a submit handle only to INPUT_SURFACE, while registry presentation_submit_without_handle (ADR-0002) says subscribing confers nothing. The registry wins; the GDD AC needs rewording. ADR-0003's closed violation set also omitted SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, which the same AC requires.

Hash-cache invalidation: ADR-0004 exposes touch_serial and recommends it to ADR-0005 because a quantised write (Graph LS-20, Emitter EM-26, Web Map WM-2) changes a block without marking a key. ADR-0005 decides; the D.12 wording sync is conditional on it. D.12 makes the cache diagnostics-only, so the stake is a stale diagnostics value.

The missed-mark audit covers only persist blocks (block_hash returns BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN for non-persist blocks) and cannot see a wrong key of a declared kind; quiet_writes_allowed blocks (Graph, Emitter, Body, Suit, Controller, Sanity) are covered only by per-mutator exact-key tests and the QUIET_WRITE_TICKS counter. Release exports detect nothing at run time. ADR-0005 may offer a hash for non-persist blocks.

Kind numbers for Emitter, Suit, Web Map, Attention and Controller families are unnumbered in their GDDs; each owner ADR fixes them (distinct within a block); a CI key-space consistency test per owner is specified.
Graph composite family L/<loop>/<anchor> must pack into the 32-bit id; ADR-0011 fixes the packing and range check.
PERCEPTION_OUT block batches (sanity.perception) should reach only the Perception Filter and Debug; delivery here is class-based, so a subscribe-time rule belongs to ADR-0009 or ADR-0024.

UNVERIFIED engine facts (settled by KRN-LAT-02 and ADR-0003's KRN-CTX-06 on a release export): PackedInt64Array.has/sort/bsearch/fill release-template cost; that signals emit in connection order (never relied on); behaviour of a subscriber that aborts on a script error in release; typed Dictionary[StringName, int] (4.4, post-cutoff) with a plain-Dictionary fallback.
Six event integers fit every current GDD payload (BODY_TRANSFER is exactly six after splitting weld/detach/pod into three event kinds); a longer payload needs a seventh slot or a second event.

A fault leaves half-applied blocks visible through read views with no notification (the faulting tick's marks are discarded per KRN-NOT-01); accepted because the fault screen replaces the play view, but worth confirming with the presentation owners.
Joint review pending: engine specialist and technical director have not reviewed this ADR; Review Log reads 'pending (joint review)'.
